reason: E1 supports the ductility loss at intermediate temperatures. E3 directly supports segregation/nanoclustering leading to decohesion in the same alloy system. However, E2 is about friction and wear in UHV and does not support any key premise; it is misrepresented. The causal link from decohesion to macroscopic brittle behavior is stated in E3 but not experimentally demonstrated there.
premises: Single-phase FCC HEAs lose ductility at intermediate temperatures (400–800°C)
Grain boundary segregation and nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, Mn occur at elevated temperature in CoCrFeMnNi
Such segregation/nanoclustering leads to grain boundary decohesion
Grain boundary decohesion causes brittle behavior and loss of toughness
The mechanism is distinct from conventional alloy embrittlement
